object_context: For the F(a)=1 branch of Seregin arXiv:2606.29468v1 Theorem 3.1, audit whether the ancient Euler limit's scale-critical local bounds (3.5), Euler equation (3.6), local energy inequality (3.7), and nontriviality (3.8), together with the exact local convergence produced by the blow-up passage, are sufficient to close a global rigidity argument without an additional tail/no-incoming-flux certificate.
problem_signature: ancient Euler solution on R^3 x (-infinity,0)
structural_coordinates: source equation changes from viscous Navier-Stokes to inviscid Euler in the limit
for each fixed a, Seregin records strong local L_{3nu}, weak-star L_{2,infinity}, and weak gradient L2 convergence
F(a)=1 gives sup_a [a^-1 local kinetic energy + a^-2 pressure L3/2 + a^-1 spacetime gradient L2] bounded
a standard spatial cutoff on B_R has |grad phi_R|=O(R^-1) and a parabolic temporal cutoff has |partial_t phi_R|=O(R^-2)
standard interpolation from A/E yields scale-critical spacetime L3 control of order R^2
pressure-velocity work has the same R^2 scale before the cutoff gradient
the resulting large-cutoff local-energy error is O(R), not o(1)
fixed-R convergence is not uniform tail tightness and does not justify exchanging k->infinity with R->infinity
backward uniqueness for Navier-Stokes is not an admissible Euler rigidity closure
Type-I and Type-II source classes remain separate
equivalent_formulations: Flux formulation: prove that the annular Euler energy/pressure flux through radius R vanishes as R->infinity.
Tightness formulation: obtain a k-uniform tail certificate on rescaled Navier-Stokes fields before passing k->infinity.
Quantifier formulation: justify an exchange or diagonalization between fixed-radius compactness and the large-radius limit.
Rigidity formulation: find an Euler Liouville theorem whose hypotheses are exactly inherited from Seregin's F=1 source class.
